new_statements.quote: As would be typical for a stress system, every phonological word in Shiwiar only has one primary accent which is usually associated with a single vowel, as in (5.184). This is manifested phonetically by higher pitch, longer duration and increased amplitude compared to other vowels in the word. [...] Accent placement in Shiwiar is not predictable based on general phonotactic or metric principles. Even the claim that accent is lexically specified (i.e. that each word has an accent on a particular syllable) is hard to uphold because there is so much variation – both in the speech of a single person and across speakers. It is therefore difficult to make generalisations, but there are certain tendencies that should be noted.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Each phonological word carries exactly one primary accent (culminative; realised by pitch, duration and intensity, with tone-like rightward spreading of high pitch under some suffixes such as the vocative). Its position is not derivable from syllable count, weight or any metrical principle and is at best lexically/morphologically determined with considerable free variation: nouns tend to accent a root vowel, certain suffixes attract the accent, adding nominal suffixes/enclitics often shifts the accent one vowel rightward (júmi 'water' vs jumí=nʲ), and accent shift alone can mark case (íkʲam 'forest' vs ikʲám LOC). Fast's SIL descriptions of Peruvian Achual/Corrientes Jívaro (1975, DEL 20 p. 9; DEL 21 p. 3; 1974 annex) independently state that accent is phonemic, give minimal pairs (núŋka 'tierra' vs nuŋká 'en la tierra', wári 'rápido' vs warí '¿qué?'), and say explicitly 'no hay regla para prever dónde debe caer el énfasis'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Kohlberger: only one primary accent per phonological word; no secondary stress described, but the accent's high pitch can spread over all following vowels in certain morphological configurations (e.g. vocative umát͡ʃírú). Fast 1975 (DEL 21 p. 18; DEL 20 sec. 3.3): a secondary accent exists, sometimes as strong as the primary and distinguished from it by (lower) tone; its position is not predictable.
new_statements.exceptions: Tendencies rather than rules: a limited set of suffixes attract accent; in verbs either root or certain suffixes bear it; compounds and whole noun phrases form one accent domain and strongly tend to be accented on the last vowel of the first word even when that vowel is unaccented in isolation (hápa 'red brocket' vs hapá_jãwãã 'cougar'); reduplications accent the last vowel of the first copy; monosyllabic roots double their vowel in isolation. Accent shift marks locative/genitive on some nouns and vocative (Fast dictionary: vocative = accent on last syllable).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word including enclitics; compounds and noun phrases count as a single accent domain with one accent. Kohlberger describes the Shiwiar variety (Ecuador, Conambo/Corrientes basin); Fast describes Peruvian Achual (Huasaga) and Corrientes-river Jívaro; all fall under Glottolog achu1248 / ISO acu, and all agree that accent is contrastive and not positionally fixed.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog achu1248 / ISO acu lumps Achuar and Shiwiar (Kohlberger 2020: 22 fn. c notes this explicitly and treats them as distinct varieties). The quoted modern statement (Kohlberger 2020) describes Shiwiar as spoken in Juyuintsa and other Ecuadorian Shiwiar villages (Conambo/Corrientes basin). The SIL sources describe Peruvian varieties: Fast 1975 DEL 20 = 'achual' of the Río Huasaga (Loreto), Fast 1975 DEL 21 = 'jíbaro del río Corrientes' (1961-62 data, ~500 speakers, Arboleda), both catalogued by SIL/Glottolog under acu/achu1248. All three agree: contrastive (phonemic) accent, one per word, position not predictable by rule.

sources.citation: Fast Mowitz, Gerhard. 1975 [1962; annex dated Feb. 1974]. Descripción comparativa de los rasgos distintivos fonémicos de varios idiomas de la familia lingüística jíbara, with Anexo 'El acento en la familia lingüística jíbara: comparación de vocablos entre las lenguas aguaruna, huambisa y achual' (Datos Etno-Lingüísticos 21). Lima: ILV. SIL archives item 30278.
sources.note: III.A p. 11: 'En los cuatro idiomas de la familia lingüística jíbara el acento es fonémico' with Corrientes Achuar pairs; p. 12: Corrientes Jívaro has a secondary accent often as strong as the primary, distinguished by tone. Anexo (1974, PDF p. 42): 'la localización del énfasis o acento es importante por ser de carácter fonémico... no hay regla para prever dónde debe caer el énfasis'; most Aguaruna/Huambisa/Achual cognates carry accent on the same syllable but which differ cannot be predicted; comparative accent-marked word lists follow.

sources.citation: Fast Mowitz, Gerhard. 1975 [analysis dated 21 May 1962]. Análisis tentativo del sistema fonológico del idioma jíbaro del río Corrientes (Datos Etno-Lingüísticos 21). Lima: ILV. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 30179.
sources.note: Sec. III p. 3: 'El acento constituye un contraste fonémico' with minimal pairs (hę́a 'casa' vs hęá 'a la casa', wári 'rápido' vs warí '¿qué?', núŋka vs nuŋká...). Sec. 7 p. 18 'Relaciones de acento y tono': 'Hemos descubierto que el acento es fonémico. Sin embargo hay otro acento secundario, que a veces es tan fuerte como el acento primordial, pero se distingue por el tono'; followed by an indented quotation from Turner (on Jívaro/Shuar of Macuma) which contains the 'preferred placement: first syllable of a vowel-final disyllable, otherwise second syllable' generalisation -- that is Turner's…

sources.note: 'Alfabeto' notes (p. 16): 'El acento ortográfico, en algunos casos, es lo único que distingue el significado de dos palabras, por ejemplo: kuchi "chancho"; kuchi "cuchillo"' (accents lost in scanned). Grammar notes: vocative differs from genitive in that 'el acento recae en la última sílaba'; possession sometimes marked only by accent shift to the following syllable (nuwe 'arcilla' / nuwé 'su arcilla'). No general placement rule.

sources.note: Sec. III 'Fonemas suprasegmentales', 3.2 (p. 9): 'El acento constituye otro contraste fonémico' with minimal pairs (núwë 'arcilla' vs nuwë́ 'su mujer', núŋka 'tierra' vs nuŋká 'en la tierra', héa 'casa' vs heá 'en la casa'...); 'No se ha observado un contraste fonémico causado por el tono. Las sílabas que llevan el acento también tienen un tono alto.' 3.3: intonation patterns with a weaker secondary accent. No placement rule given; orthography table (p. ~20) says accent is written only on homophone pairs distinguished solely by accent.
